title: Which German Cities Have an Umweltzone? Check Before You Drive
description: Low-emission zones cover most larger German cities. See where you can't enter without the green sticker, and sort it out before you leave home.
excerpt: Berlin, Munich, Stuttgart, Cologne — plus dozens of smaller towns. Without the green sticker, the city centre is simply closed to you.
content:
The Umweltzone stopped being a big-city thing years ago. More than fifty German cities now run low-emission zones, and almost all of them apply the same rule: green sticker only.

## Where you'll hit one

Berlin has the largest zone, covering everything inside the S-Bahn ring, so any trip into the centre crosses it. Munich's zone sits inside the Mittlerer Ring, Stuttgart covers essentially the whole city, and Cologne, Düsseldorf and Frankfurt cover the centre plus surrounding districts. Smaller places catch drivers out too: Heidelberg, Freiburg, Erfurt, Halle, Magdeburg, Osnabrück.

## How to spot the zone from the driver's seat

A round sign with a red border reading UMWELTZONE marks the start, with a plate underneath showing the green sticker. The end of the zone uses the same sign crossed out. There's no barrier and no gate — just cameras and police checks. The 100-euro fine often arrives months later, by post, at your home address.

## What to do before you set off

The sticker is a one-off and stays valid for the life of the car, so you deal with it once. The simplest route is online via [nemeckaplaketa.cz](https://nemeckaplaketa.cz): upload your vehicle registration document, pay by card, and the sticker arrives in the post. No hunting down a TÜV or DEKRA station on arrival.

Driving to Germany this year? Order it now rather than the night before — delivery takes a few days.
